etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Alteration of devest, from Middle French devester (“strip of possessions”), from Old French desvestir, from des- (“dis-”) + vestir (“to clothe”).
senses: (transitive) To strip, deprive, or dispossess (someone) of something (such as a right, passion, privilege, or prejudice).
(transitive, finance) To sell off or be rid of through sale, especially of a subsidiary.
